plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Small, nodding white bells with delicate green-marked inner petals push up through frost, leaf litter and sometimes snow. Drifts of them carpet woodland floors and old churchyards. They are among the first flowers of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to February, and sometimes earlier in mild winters
plants.location: Woodlands, parks and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make their own natural antifreeze-like compounds and can raise their flower stems through frozen ground. They also contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medicine for early Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Spicy-sweet, fragrant blossoms open on bare branches while winter still grips the landscape. The flowers range from pure white to deep pink-red, often with a darker calyx. Each tree looks like a cloud of blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early January through February in the mild climate of its native Yangtze region, and from late February into March in colder parts of Japan
plants.location: Central China and Japan, in gardens, orchards and plum-blossom parks
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a traditional symbol of perseverance and the coming of spring in East Asian culture. They bloom before cherry blossoms and long before the tree's leaves appear.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs burst into rose-like flowers of satin petals around a boss of golden stamens. The flowers can be single, semi-double or fully double. In late winter they brighten the garden when little else is in color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, typically February to April, with some varieties opening earlier
plants.location: Gardens in Japan and the southeastern United States, where winters are mild
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. It has been cultivated for centuries, and thousands of named cultivars exist.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry round, umbrella-like clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere summer they make a bold, cooling show of blue.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, December to February
plants.location: Eastern Cape and the coastal regions of South Africa, where it is native, and gardens across the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, the African lily is not a true lily. It belongs to the amaryllis family, and its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower.'
